name: Taylor's Green

layers.essential_history: [[c:The village board says Taylor's Green is an old street of the hamlet of Southorp, which declined after the Black Death in 1349. The farm drawn next to it on the board is Long Lane Farm, from the early 18th century.]]
layers.deeper_history: [[c:The board says Long Lane was the link between the main village and Southorp. Some of the stone and gravel used to build the church was quarried from the fields beyond Southorp Street.]]
layers.mystery: [[c:Journal page: you reach a field where the estate's animals once grazed. ]]Mr Vale[[c: swears he spent the whole afternoon here.]]

puzzle.title: Can it be true?
puzzle.intro: Mr Vale[[c: says he was out here all afternoon. Check his story against the sketch map note.]]
material: MR VALE[[c: SAYS: "I left the stable yard at the second bell, walked to the far barn, spent one bell there and walked back. I was in the yard again by the third bell."]]
[[c:SKETCH MAP NOTE: it takes one bell to walk from the stable yard to the far barn, and one bell to walk back.]]
puzzle.question: [[c:At the earliest, which bell could he have been back in the yard? Type a number.]]
hints: [[c:Count the walk there, the time at the barn, and the walk back.]]
[[c:He left at the second bell. One bell there, one bell at the barn, one bell back.]]
puzzle.reveal: [[c:He couldn't be back before the fifth bell, so his story about the third doesn't hold up.]]
puzzle.fallback: [[c:You don't need to be in the field for this one. If the alpacas are out, say hello!]]

evidence: Mr Vale[[c:'s story doesn't add up. He couldn't have been back by the third bell.]]
directions_to_next: [[c:Head north-east for about 170 metres to the cemetery gatehouse. Look for the gatehouse at the cemetery entrance. Keep to the pavements and paths, and look from the road only.]]
notes: Exact paths and how this joins the cemetery and Big Green are not known yet.
